title: Writing for a new voice and Bill Berry's first nights in the band
summary: Duke wrote for individual players and tested newcomers; Bill Berry found cigarette-burned parts and was told to find a note.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

Yeah. Well, Bill Berry has a funny story. When he came in the band. Well, he wasn't used to these personalities, you know, so there were no trumpet parts for him and those that he saw had cigarette burnings all over them, you know, and Cat and the guys, they wouldn't say anything to him, so he said he was really confused. Said, "This is the greatest band in the world, but I don't understand it," you know? So he would -- he'd just sit there and Duke would -- told him, he says, "Put your horn to your mouth. Dress my bandstand up, whether you've got anything to play or not." And then later on Duke kept telling him -- he'd say, "What should I play on this?" He says, "Find a note." Then he was
testing his ear.
Uh-huh.
You know, that's what he was really doing. "Find a note. See what you can squeeze in there." Then he could find out what latitude he had to work with, you know?
Uh-huh.
And eventually he got -- he got some stuff around Bill.
Yes.
You know, he found him.

And Bill told me on his first night with the band, he didn't know, not having a book, didn't know what to play and asked Cat what he should put on the end of the number, and Cat said, "Pick a note that sounds wrong and play it."
